surface: A piece’s feedback: what the course says after a showing
where: School, Coursework, each piece’s card under Feedback, and the Feedback notice after class
why: Read in order in the baseline’s 24 runs, five courses spoke one frame: “It’s at 50% now, and the note is taken at 75%” 451 times from 21 courses; a new note named its part twice (“Your lines held it back most. The lines weren’t secure…”); card labels stood as prose subjects (“the note on Built On”); a single point of tiredness made a Strong piece “strong despite the day”; and a part left unfinished was answered with a step beyond it.
changes: Composed by situation in five course voices (direct, warm, exacting, patient, brisk; `VOICE_OF`), two first-year courses of one discipline never sharing one. A new note runs into its own words; a note given before says where its part stands and the rule that puts it right (“It’s at 50%. A piece shown with it at 75% or more puts the note right.”), never “taken”; a first Strong, a best and a piece strong despite a day that cost two points or more stop at the acknowledgment; a part left unfinished is answered by the steps that finish it; every move names the new band; a day and the band are said once; the words are chosen by the shapes and frames the course said lately, with no draw from the game’s randomness.

evidence.ref: tests/feedback-voices.test.ts: 'is said whole and true: no card label as a subject, no "taken", no two colons in a sentence, the date and figures it has, and a step only where the situation gives one'
tests/feedback-voices.test.ts: 'says the same facts in words no other voice uses: no whole message, and no first sentence, shared'
tests/feedback-voices.test.ts: 'stops at a first Strong, a best and a strong piece despite the day, holds back the step where what held a piece has a remedy, and gives it at a plateau'
tests/feedback-voices.test.ts: 'says a day once: a move from the piece shown the day a slipped note was put right says the day in one place'
tests/language-dynamic.test.ts: 'a teacher’s note on an unchanged weakness says it was said before, how often, and when; never as a new discovery'

surface: The feedback card’s label and the note’s heading
where: School, Coursework, Feedback on each piece: the label beside it (A New Note, Still There, What Held It Back)
why: A piece held back by something other than its notes, or by nothing, carried the label of a note (“A New Note”) though no note was given, so the label and the words beneath it disagreed.
changes: `kindLabel`: “What Held It Back” where a limit held a prepared piece, “Nothing Held It Back” where nothing did; a note keeps its kind’s label. Labels stay the same words every time they apply.

evidence.ref: tests/evidence-g24-school.test.ts: 'draws the note on the Coursework tab: the skill note new, then taken, shown again and marked taken in the ledger; and the objective a note put first, with why'

surface: Your Notes: every note given, and where each stands
why: Read on the workload save at 1440, each note is a line a player can scan: its subject, how often, first and last given, and Open or Taken with the day. The ledger’s rehearsal note was named “Time On Its Feet”, a scene’s word, though it counts Voice I’s daily practice, Speech’s drills and the movement score’s rehearsal too.
changes: The rehearsal note is “Rehearsal” (`DIM_SUBJECT`), and the feedback names it in prose by what it is in every course (`DIM_WORDS`), with the piece’s own name for it after (“Here that’s the daily practice, at 23%.”).

evidence.ref: tests/evidence2-b11.test.ts: 'PLAYER JOURNEY: Your Work So Far at the end of a played school, dismissed by 20 December 2027: every section as the records it reads give it, worked out here, and a reload the same'

surface: A Note That Keeps Coming Back and Another Way At It
where: School, Coursework, a piece’s card, where a note has come back three times or more
why: Each way is named as its control is and says what it costs in time and what it works on (“a half-hour drill of it, once a day”); the feedback points to it by the card’s own heading, so the player can find the control from the words.

evidence.ref: tests/direction.test.ts: 'names what the part’s forecast shows, where, with several ways at it; worked, it keeps its way and its evidence'
